definitions: A species of bacteria that can cause meningitis and other forms of meningococcal disease.
A gram-negative diplococcus responsible for meningococcal meningitis.
examples: Neisseria meningitidis was identified in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Vaccination targets specific serogroups of Neisseria meningitidis.
The spread of Neisseria meningitidis can occur through respiratory droplets.
